findings.evidence: `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:539` calls `loadTable(... addUserFilterCondition(sqlLoadUserTable, userList), p.decodeUserTableRow(userList))`. `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:885` disables SQL filtering when `len(userList)==0 || len(userList)>1024`, so the query becomes unfiltered. Unlike other decoders (e.g. `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1118`), `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:980` (`decodeUserTableRow`) never checks `userList` before inserting into `p.user`, so an unfiltered scan materializes all `mysql.user` rows. This is reachable via periodic/all reloads when acceleration is enabled: `pkg/domain/domain.go:1992` sets `event.All=true` periodically and `pkg/domain/domain.go:2006` routes `event.All` to `h.UpdateAllActive()`, which always calls `h.updateUsers(userList)` even when empty (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:2168`).
findings.fix: Add the same guard used by other decoders to `decodeUserTableRow`: before inserting, if `userList != nil` and `value.User` not in `userList`, `return nil`. Also consider short-circuiting `Handle.updateUsers` when `len(userList)==0` to avoid full table scans for the empty-active-users case.
findings.impact: With `@@global.tidb_accelerate_user_creation_update=ON`, `UpdateAllActive()` (periodic `event.All` or etcd-triggered reload-all) can transiently load and allocate the full `mysql.user` cache even when updating no users (empty active set) or only a subset (>1024 users) of a very large user table (e.g. 2M users). This can reintroduce large memory spikes/GC jitter and potentially OOM, undermining the PR’s goal.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `addUserFilterCondition` still returns unfiltered SQL for `len(userList)==0 || >1024` and `decodeUserTableRow` still lacks a `userList` membership check, so the behavior persists.
findings.verify: Enable `tidb_accelerate_user_creation_update=ON`, create a large `mysql.user` population, and trigger `privReloadEvent` with `event.All=true` (or wait for the periodic tick). Confirm that before the fix, `UpdateAllActive()` performs an unfiltered `SELECT ... FROM mysql.user` when active user set is empty or >1024, and materializes all users in the temporary privilege struct; after the fix, `decodeUserTableRow` skips non-target users and the temporary `p.user` only contains the intended `userList` (and roles) even when SQL filtering is disabled.
findings.what: `UpdateAllActive`/`Update` incremental privilege reload can still materialize the entire `mysql.user` table when the target user set is empty or >1024, because `decodeUserTableRow` ignores `userList` while SQL filtering is disabled in that case.

subject: privilege, domain: reduce the memory jitter of privilege reload activity for 2M users (#59487)
summary: This commit switches privilege reload to use internal SQL streaming via a sys session pool to reduce memory jitter. However, in the accelerated (partial) reload path, `mysql.user` decoding does not honor the `userList` filter when SQL filtering is intentionally disabled for empty/large user sets, so `UpdateAllActive()` can still transiently load/allocate the full user table and reintroduce large memory spikes.
